  • Production is deliberately disarmed - healthy, running the accepted release, schedules off until ARN arms it.

Support

When something breaks

Every alert maps to a written action.
  • The runbook starts where support starts - an alert fired, what do I do, page by page.
  • Alerts arrive in a Microsoft Teams channel, with email as a backstop, and each one maps to an action.
  • The support model says which vendor owns which failure.
  • The escalation matrix is a template - the roles are laid out; ARN fills in its own names and hours.

Dependencies

Where it depends on ARN

Six state road-authority feeds are wired. Two are switched on, and the rest need one thing each from ARN.
  • New South Wales answers reliably. Queensland answers on a shared demonstration key that gets rate-limited, and is refused in development. It needs a dedicated authority key.
  • Tasmania and Western Australia answer and parse, but sit switched off. They need a setting in Bulletin rules, nothing else.
  • South Australia refuses the platform's address. It needs one allowlist entry from their road-operations team.
  • Playout - the audio reaches the share. The station clock decides whether it airs.
Handover to ARN · 4 September 2026
Boundaries

What is read-only on purpose

  • Emergency services. The console shows emergency records once ARN holds a DataQuoll key and the licensing is settled. It is display-only by design: those records never reach a script and cannot go to air, so on-air behaviour is the same with or without the key.
  • Every bulletin still waits for a person. Nothing reaches air on its own, in any environment.
  • Alerts land in a Microsoft Teams channel. That path runs inside the same subscription as the platform, so it cannot report the subscription being down - an ARN-owned email or SMS address is the only route that survives that.
